Current bid stands at $132,964 with the auction ending in 3 days.

contradictions.detail: The listing presents the car as a Carrera 4 widebody, but the Carfax quoted in the listing identifies it as a 1994 911 RS America. The VIN sequence and sticker type 964 150 fit the listing's description, which suggests a Carfax misread, but the factory widebody claim should be confirmed with a Porsche CoA.
The body text cites Midnight Blue Metallic as L37C, while the option-sticker decode lists L39C.
The text says the engine was overhauled 'between 202 and 2025' (a typo). The owner summary says work ran from 2/29/24 to 12/2025.

critical_evidence.evidence: An owner-typed engine rebuild summary is photographed. It lists ARP head studs and rod bolts, resized rods, Dougherty reground cams, a head valve job with new exhaust guides, rings, chains, tensioners, rails, a rebuilt oil cooler, and new oil and fuel lines. 'Records' and refurbishment photos are said to exist. No machine-shop invoices with line items or shop names were examined here.
No post-rebuild compression or leakdown numbers are provided. A dealer 'safety inspection' is mentioned without results.
The owner summary lists 'New distributor timing belt' and 'New caps and rotors' during the 2024-2025 work. No dated receipt was examined here.
No scan or pressure test of the C4 ABS/ABD hydraulic unit or accumulator. Warning-light status is not stated.
A photo with the lower pan removed shows clean, dry case seams, sump, exhaust and heat exchangers. Battery tray, front trunk floor, oil cooler lines and torsion tube were not examined here.

documentation.rationale: The identity and terms half is present: VIN, a photographed option sticker, clean Carfax, NY title and $0 dealer fees. The maintenance half is partial: an owner-typed rebuild summary, refurbishment photos and an underside photo. Itemized machine-shop invoices, leakdown results and a C4 scan are not shown. The Carfax model misidentification and the odometer-exempt title weaken verifiability.

condition.rationale: Photos show a fresh interior, clean engine bay, a dry, clean underside and good paint, and the tires are 2023/2024. The stated faults are minor: disabled AM/FM/CD functions and a touched-up hood chip. No PPI, leakdown or C4 hydraulic scan supports an 8+, and the refurbishment has only about 1,200 miles on it.

price_value.rationale: No fair-value estimate or comps are provided. The current bid is $131,964 with four days left and 1,314 watchers, so the hammer will likely be higher. The price rests entirely on the refurbishment paperwork, and the key invoices were not examined here. Relative to Jason's stated budget band ($10,000-$19,000 ideal, $35,000 max price), value to this buyer is poor.

mission_fit.rationale: It is a genuine keeper-grade manual 964, but its price level sits entirely outside the stated budget band. It conflicts directly with the cash-preservation, accelerated-bridge situation and does not solve the bridge problem.

logistics.rationale: The car is in North Salem, NY, and the dealer has shipping and storage in place. In-person viewing is offered only on 9/29, the close day, with no PPI offer stated. California smog feasibility with reground cams is unconfirmed.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: It combines a claimed factory widebody (one of 267 NA coupes), a five-speed manual, Midnight Blue over Cashmere, Exclusive-program supple leather, a rootwood knob and Cup wheels. The paint and interior are refinished rather than original, which trims originality.

evidence.mission_note: This is a keeper-only car: a rare manual widebody 964 that would reward a long-term owner. At a current bid of $131,964 against a stated max price of $35,000, it conflicts directly with the current cash-preservation, accelerated-bridge strategy.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes the VIN, a photographed option sticker, a clean-Carfax snapshot, and an owner-typed rebuild summary. The summary covers the M64's main weak points: ARP head studs and rod bolts, valve work with new guides, chains and tensioners, a rebuilt oil cooler, and new oil and fuel lines. The underside photo shows a clean, dry case after the work, and the tires are recent 2023/2024 Michelins. Observed issues are the Carfax listing the car as an RS America, a paint-code inconsistency (L37C vs L39C), a full strip-and-respray with replaced windshield and body parts, and an odometer-exempt title with replaced odometer gears. The stereo's AM/FM/CD functions are disabled. Still open: itemized machine-shop invoices, post-rebuild leakdown numbers, a C4 ABS/ABD hydraulic scan, a CoA confirming factory widebody status, and California smog compatibility of the reground cams. No PPI access is stated, and in-person viewing falls on the close day. The current bid of $131,964, with four days remaining and heavy watcher interest, places the car in a price tier far above the stated budget band.
evidence.next_action: Ask 1600veloce for the complete itemized refurbishment invoices, any leakdown results and a Porsche CoA, and whether an independent PPI with an ABS/ABD scan can be done before the 9/29 close.
